blocks.source: Vol IV, Closed-Loop Evaluation, § What a Physical Success Rate Measures
blocks.md: A latch-manipulation policy that reliably opens a door during morning bench tests can jam repeatedly when confronted with a strike plate displaced by only three millimeters. Its measured success rate does not belong to the neural network weights in isolation; it characterizes the coupled dynamical system formed by the policy, the mechanical plant, the onboard compute platform, the physical environment, and the trial protocol itself.

questions.q: The section **What a Physical Success Rate Measures** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A physical success rate is the expectation of a frozen outcome predicate over a declared distribution of trial conditions (initial state, environment, unit, frozen policy and permission parameters), so it belongs to that population and to no other.
Replay resets the input to the recorded state each step, so a heading bias with a tiny angular MSE can spend a 15 cm aisle clearance in seconds once the loop closes.
A finite record supports a claim only if the target ODD, its weights, approximately independent draws, a frozen predicate, and the full denominator are fixed before the first run.
A simulator earns authority to screen candidates only through a paired sim-and-real benchmark scored for rank inversions, and even then it filters, never certifies.

questions.explanation: This section develops **Predeclared trial protocol**: A finite record supports a claim only if the target ODD, its weights, approximately independent draws, a frozen predicate, and the full denominator are fixed before the first run.

points: **Closed-loop trial**: A trial of the complete controller and plant in which actions determine later observations and the declared outcome is scored.
